title: fix(sedreplace): a multi-file apply over @stdin patterns fails midway and lands on a subset of the planned files
description:
# 🌙 dream: `sedreplace --mode apply` over @stdin patterns reports a failure and lands on a subset of the files its plan listed

- kind = reseed
- owner = ehmpathy/rhachet-roles-ehmpathy (mechanic `claude.tools/sedreplace.sh`)
- caught 2026-09-26

## .the cue that fired

three applies in one session, each after a clean plan run, each on a multi-file glob with both
patterns fed via `printf 'old\0new' | … --old @stdin --new @stdin`:

| the edit | plan said | apply said | landed on |
|---|---|---|---|
| `(error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code` → `getFsErrorCode(error)` | 3 files | `💥 failed with an error` | 1 of 3 |
| `tail: TAIL_OF_TEST,` → `+ msOfTimeout: null,` | 2 sites | `💥 failed with an error` | 0 of 2 |
| a third @stdin apply the same session | n files | `💥 failed with an error` | partial |

single-file @stdin applies the same day landed in full, so the defect tracks the MULTI-FILE path.

## .the gap, precisely

- the plan and the apply disagree on what they touch, and the apply does not say which files it
  wrote before it failed — so a caller cannot tell a clean no-op from a half-applied rename
- a half-applied rename is the worst outcome a bulk tool can leave: the tree type-checks in one
  file and not the next, and the failure message names no file
- the skill's own guarantee reads *"fail-fast on errors"*; a partial write before the error is
  not fail-fast, it is fail-midway

## .the shape of the fix

- read stdin ONCE into a buffer before the per-file loop; the likeliest cause is a per-file
  re-read of a stdin that the first file already drained (the NUL split then yields an empty
  `old`, which matches naught or errors)
- stage every file's new content first, then write them all; on any error write none
- on failure, name the file and the error; on success, list each file written (the plan already does)
- clamp it: an integration test over a 3-file temp repo with both patterns via @stdin, which
  asserts all 3 files change or none do

## .why it is not done in this round

the skill belongs to another repo (`rhachet-roles-ehmpathy`), so this tree cannot adopt the fix.
the workaround here was to verify each apply with `grepsafe` and finish the misses by hand with Edit.
